result: Individual MELT motifs in Spc105 have different Bub3-Bub1 binding affinities determined by their amino acid sequences, with consensus 'MELT' motifs (#2, #6) recruiting more Bub1 than divergent motifs (#4 'IDLT'). Just one strong MELT motif is sufficient to maintain prolonged mitotic arrest in nocodazole-treated cells.
evaluation: Claims C19-C27 are well-supported by experimental data showing differential Bub1 recruitment (C21-C23, Figure 1C) and flow cytometry demonstrating SAC strength (C21, C24, Figure 1D). The sequence-to-function relationship is validated by the rescue experiment where converting motif #4 to consensus sequence improved both Bub1 recruitment and SAC strength (C25).

result: Under benomyl-induced microtubule stress (creating small numbers of unattached kinetochores), at least two strong MELT motifs are necessary for cell survival and maximal population growth, whereas one or two strong motifs are insufficient to prevent premature anaphase onset.
evaluation: Claims C28-C40 are supported by multiple complementary assays: chromosome biorientation tracking (C30-C33, Figure 2A), anaphase timing (C34-C35, Figure 2B), and population growth curves in benomyl (C36-C38, Figure 2C). The data consistently show that Spc105 mutants with fewer strong MELT motifs exhibit weaker SAC under physiologically relevant conditions with small numbers of unattached kinetochores.

result: The amino acid sequence, not the position of MELT motifs in the Spc105 phosphodomain, determines their SAC signaling activity.
evaluation: Claim C41 is supported by position-swap experiments (Figure 2E) showing that swapping the positions of motifs #1-3 and #4-6 did not change benomyl sensitivity patterns, demonstrating that sequence rather than position is the key determinant of MELT motif function.

result: Spc105 containing more than one strong MELT motif is essential for accurate chromosome segregation during normal cell division, as demonstrated by significantly elevated chromosome missegregation rates in Spc105#4-6 mutants compared to wild-type and even SAC-null strains.
evaluation: Claims C42-C45 are supported by colony sectoring assays (Figure 2F) showing significantly higher chromosome loss rates in Spc105#4-6 mutants. The explanation involving reduced Sgo1 recruitment (C44) is supported by supplementary data (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C-D), though this adds complexity beyond pure SAC strength effects.

result: SAC strength measured by duration of mitotic arrest in nocodazole-treated cells (with large, constant numbers of unattached kinetochores) does not predict the ability of the SAC to ensure genome stability under physiological conditions, because cumulative signaling from many kinetochores masks defects in individual kinetochore signaling.
evaluation: Claims C46, C102-C105 are supported by the contrasting results between nocodazole experiments (where Spc105#4-6 appears normal, Figure 2—figure supplement 3A) and benomyl/normal growth experiments (where the same mutant shows clear defects, Figures 2C, 2F). This demonstrates that the standard nocodazole assay can be misleading for assessing physiological SAC function.

result: A diminishing gradient of Mps1 kinase activity extends from the CH-domains toward the centromere in bioriented kinetochores, continuing to phosphorylate MELT motifs but not Bub1. This residual activity primes the SAC for silencing but is insufficient to induce anaphase; PP1 is required for timely anaphase onset.
evaluation: Claims C51-C65 are supported by FRET data (C53-C54, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), phosphodomain tethering experiments showing position-dependent Bub3 recruitment (C55-C59, Figure 3A-C), and the absence of Mad1 recruitment when tethered distally (C60, Figure 3D). The interpretation that reduced Mps1 activity primes but doesn't complete SAC silencing (C64-C65) is a reasonable inference from the data.

result: PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of Bub1 contributes to SAC silencing, but MELT motif dephosphorylation by PP1 has a stronger impact because dephosphorylating one residue in a MELT motif prevents both Bub3-Bub1 and Mad1 recruitment, whereas multiple Bub1 sites must be dephosphorylated to inhibit Mad1 recruitment.
evaluation: Claims C66-C76 are supported by experiments with spc105RASA bub1453A,455A double mutants (Figure 4C) showing that mutating Bub1 phosphosites partially rescues viability but doesn't eliminate SAC activity or Mad1 recruitment. The logic comparing efficiency of MELT vs Bub1 dephosphorylation (C73-C76) is sound given the mechanistic differences.

result: A hyperactive Spc105 variant (#16) with six high-affinity MELT motifs shows defective SAC silencing (14% longer doubling time) without conferring advantages in benomyl stress, demonstrating that too many high-affinity MELT motifs impose a fitness cost.
evaluation: Claims C78-C83 are supported by data showing Bub1 retention at bioriented kinetochores (C78, Figure 5A), increased doubling time that is SAC-dependent (C79-C80, Figure 5A), and lack of advantage in benomyl (C81, Figure 5A). This demonstrates the trade-off between SAC strength and responsiveness.

result: Bub1 overexpression reveals that both Bub1 abundance and MELT motif number/affinity determine SAC responsiveness, with the hyperactive #16 variant showing disproportionately greater sensitivity to Bub1 overexpression (35-66% increase in doubling time vs 15% for wild-type).
evaluation: Claims C84-C88 are supported by Bub1 overexpression experiments (Figure 5B) showing differential effects on wild-type vs #16 strains. The quantitative differences in fold-increase of doubling time (C86) provide strong evidence that MELT motif affinity modulates SAC responsiveness to Bub1 levels.

result: Only weak MELT motifs (#4-6), not strong motifs (#1-3), can suppress the lethality of spc105RASA (defective PP1 recruitment), suggesting that Bub3-Bub1 binding to strong MELT motifs sterically interferes with PP1-mediated dephosphorylation.
evaluation: Claims C89-C91 are supported by tetrad dissection showing differential rescue (Figure 6A). The steric interference model (C91) is a reasonable mechanistic explanation consistent with structural data (C47-C48) and the differential rescue pattern, though direct biochemical evidence for the mechanism is not provided.

result: An engineered Spc105 variant (spc105#4-6RASA) with weak MELT motifs and no PP1 recruitment demonstrates improved chromosome segregation accuracy (3 vs 18 red colonies per ~6000 for wild-type) and faster growth in benomyl, but at the cost of 20% longer doubling time under normal conditions.
evaluation: Claims C92-C98 are supported by multiple assays: fluorescence microscopy (C92, Figure 6B), flow cytometry (C93, Figure 6B), benomyl growth (C94, Figure 6C), colony sectoring (C95, Figure 6E), and doubling time measurements (C96, Figure 6D). This engineered variant demonstrates the principle that SAC strength and responsiveness can be balanced. However, C97 acknowledges that the SAC silencing defect explanation needs experimental confirmation.

result: The tethered phosphodomain recruits Mad1 in spc105RASA,#4-6 cells but not wild-type, demonstrating that reduced Mps1 activity primes the SAC for silencing by enabling PP1 to prevent Mad1 recruitment through Bub1 dephosphorylation.
evaluation: Claims C99-C101 are supported by tethering experiments (Figure 6F) showing differential Mad1 recruitment and growth defects in rapamycin. This provides direct evidence for the model that PP1 prevents SAC activation from the tethered phosphodomain by dephosphorylating Bub1.

result: Structural analysis suggests that Bub3-Bub1 binding sterically shields the phosphothreonine in MELT motifs from PP1, making high-affinity MELT motifs more resistant to dephosphorylation and reducing SAC responsiveness to silencing.
evaluation: Claims C47-C49, C77, C115-C116 present a mechanistic model based on structural data (C47, Figure 1B) and supported by functional data showing differential rescue by weak vs strong MELT motifs (C89-C91). While the steric interference hypothesis (C48, C115) is reasonable and consistent with all data, direct biochemical evidence for differential dephosphorylation rates is not provided. The model's predictions are well-supported (C116).

result: The balance between SAC strength and responsiveness is determined by MELT motif number and Bub3-Bub1 binding affinity, with evolutionary pressure driving both amplification of MELT motif number and sequence divergence to optimize this balance for genome stability and timely cell division.
evaluation: Claims C2-C6, C50, C106-C107, C117-C121 represent the overarching conclusions of the study. These are well-supported by the collective experimental evidence showing: (1) strong MELT motifs minimize missegregation (C3, supported by C42-C45), (2) too many strong motifs delay anaphase (C4, supported by C78-C83), (3) an engineered variant can trade responsiveness for accuracy (C5, supported by C92-C98), and (4) the evolutionary interpretation (C6, C121) is a reasonable proposal given the functional data, though it remains speculative regarding actual evolutionary mechanisms.

result: Background on SAC function and MELT motifs: The SAC maintains genome stability and ensures timely anaphase onset through a kinetochore-based signaling cascade involving Spc105 and its MELT motifs, which are phosphorylated by Mps1 to activate SAC signaling.
evaluation: Claims C1, C7-C18 represent established knowledge from the literature, appropriately cited (C8, C11, C12, C14-C18). These provide necessary context for the study and are not novel findings. The claims accurately represent prior work.

result: Summary of SAC silencing mechanisms: Microtubule attachment reduces Mps1 activity to prime SAC for silencing, PP1 dephosphorylates MELT motifs and Bub1 to complete silencing, with MELT dephosphorylation having stronger impact. Eliminating Spc105-PP1 interaction improves chromosome biorientation under stress but delays silencing under normal conditions.
evaluation: Claims C108-C114 summarize the key mechanistic findings from the Discussion section. These are well-supported by the experimental data presented in the Results (particularly claims C51-C76 and C92-C98). C108 appropriately cites prior work. These represent synthesis of the findings rather than new results.
